chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the good deed is not like the evil.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The good deed is the dissimulation (Taqiyya), and the evil is the broadcasting (of one's true state).'

And His Words, Mighty and Majestic: 'Repel the evil with that which is better.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is better is the dissimulation (Taqiyya), so if there is enmity between you and him, he becomes as if he were an intimate friend.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Dissimulation; the practice of concealing one's faith or beliefs to avoid harm or danger.
key_terms.الْإِيعَاءَةُ: Broadcasting; revealing or publicizing one's true state or faith, contrasted with dissimulation.
key_terms.عَدَاوَةٌ: Enmity; hostility or animosity between parties.
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ: Intimate friend; a close, beloved companion.

ai.seo_question: How does Shia tradition interpret 'the good deed' in Quran 41:34?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the virtue of Taqiyya by interpreting Quran 41:34, where 'the good deed' is identified as the concealment of faith and 'the evil' as its public proclamation. He further connects this to the command in 41:34 to 'repel evil with what is better,' explaining that strategic dissimulation serves to transform enmity into intimacy, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence for preserving the community during periods of persecution.
